Police operatives in Kano have arrested four suspects, including a 20-year-old woman, over the alleged abduction and murder of a 14-year-old boy, Mahmoud Auwal, in Kano State. The woman, identified as Hadiya Rukayya Auwal, was accused of hiring three men for N4.5m to kill her husband’s children, including the deceased. The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed this in a police operational success release on Monday. Iniedu stated that operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad, Kano, with support from the Technical Intelligence Unit, unravelled the killing. Iniedu identified the three other suspects as Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20; Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27; and Auwal Muhammad, 26. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The FPRO wrote, “In a major investigative breakthrough, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad Kano, assisted by the Technical Intelligence Unit, successfully unravelled the abduction and murder of 14-year-old Mahmoud Auwal. “Three suspects, Muhammad Musa Isma’il (20), Abubakar Muhammad Isah (27), and Auwal Muhammad (26), were arrested and confessed to luring the victim and snatching him. The victim’s corpse was recovered and positively identified by his parents. The police spokesperson concluded that the case had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai, Kano, for further investigation. In a separate operation, Iniedu noted that the Kano operatives arrested three men and recovered a Hyundai Elantra, valued at N14m, which had allegedly been stolen in Kano State. He added that the operation followed a complaint lodged on November 12 by one Stephanie Patrick Ogedoh over the theft of her light-blue Hyundai Elantra. The FPRO identified the suspects as Mansur Khalil, 32; Nuhu Garba, 45; and Hussaini Aminu, 55, saying operatives of the Special Intervention Squad intercepted them along Zaria Road, near Kwanar Dangora, in the Kiru Local Government Area. He noted that the vehicle was recovered and the suspects allegedly confessed to the crime. He added that the suspects implicated a receiver of the stolen vehicle, while efforts were ongoing to arrest the fleeing suspect and recover more exhibits. Iniedu concluded that the case was under investigation by the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai.
